title: std/time
summary: Exact durations, civil construction, instants, timezone conversion, parsing, formatting, arithmetic, comparison, and explicit clock access.

items.name: duration
items.summary: Construct an exact signed nanosecond duration.
items.parameters: One `duration`, integral numeric value interpreted as nanoseconds, or exact `quantity[Second]` whose magnitude is an integral number of nanoseconds.
details: The range is signed 64-bit nanoseconds: approximately ±290 years.
This pure operation reports `OutOfRange` instead of wrapping and rejects fractional nanoseconds.
items.errors: `TypeError` for incompatible values, `InvalidArgument` for non-integral nanoseconds, and `OutOfRange` outside signed 64-bit nanoseconds.
items.native: Native C accepts an existing duration, an exact signed integer, or a value-owned `Second` quantity whose nanosecond product is exactly representable. The result is returned by value without a capability or retained input pointer.

items.name: parse_duration
items.summary: Parse a compact duration containing signed decimal values and unit suffixes.
items.parameters: One `string` using `ns`, `us`/`µs`, `ms`, `s`, `m`, or `h`; components may be combined, as in `1h30m`.
details: Parsing is exact to nanoseconds and does not accept a bare number.
This pure operation follows the documented Go-style duration grammar; days and calendar months are not duration units.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-string and `ParseError` for malformed or out-of-range text.

items.name: duration_string
items.summary: Render a duration in its shortest exact unit form.
items.parameters: One `duration`.
details: The output uses `h`, `m`, `s`, `ms`, `µs`, and `ns` as needed.
The result round-trips through `parse_duration` and this operation never reads the clock.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-duration or `InvalidArgument` for wrong arity.

items.name: date
items.syntax: time.date(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, nanosecond[, location])
items.summary: Construct an instant from strictly validated Gregorian civil fields.
items.parameters: Seven integral fields and an optional `location`; omission means UTC. Years are `1..9999`, months `1..12`, seconds `0..59`, and nanoseconds `0..999999999`.
details: Invalid days and clock fields fail instead of normalizing. Leap seconds are rejected.
IANA timezone gaps fail; a repeated wall time in a DST fold selects the earlier instant. This operation is deterministic.
items.errors: `TypeError`, `InvalidArgument`, or `OutOfRange` for invalid fields or location values.
items.native: Native C accepts seven exact integral civil fields or those fields plus the UTC location value. It stores a normalized value-owned `ODatetime`; non-UTC locations are an explicit source-spanned boundary because the native ABI has no location slot.

items.name: unix
items.summary: Construct a UTC instant relative to the Unix epoch without losing nanoseconds.
items.parameters: Signed integral seconds and an optional integral nanosecond adjustment; the adjustment is normalized into the second field.
details: Negative timestamps use floor-based Unix semantics with a non-negative stored nanosecond field.
The resulting civil year must remain in `1..9999`; this operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for non-integral values and `OutOfRange` for an unsupported result.
items.native: Native C uses checked signed-integer arithmetic, normalizes an optional nanosecond adjustment with floor semantics, and stores the result in the repaired value-owned `ODatetime { seconds, nanosecond }` ABI. No clock or host capability is consulted.

items.name: unix_milli
items.summary: Construct a UTC instant from exact signed Unix milliseconds.
items.parameters: One signed integral millisecond count.
details: Conversion uses integer arithmetic; negative sub-second epochs retain their exact fraction.
The resulting civil year must remain in `1..9999`; no clock is read.
items.errors: `TypeError` for non-integral input and `OutOfRange` for an unsupported result.
items.native: Native C multiplies the exact signed millisecond count with checked arithmetic, normalizes it into seconds plus a non-negative nanosecond field, and returns a UTC `ODatetime` by value.

items.name: unix_micro
items.summary: Construct a UTC instant from exact signed Unix microseconds.
items.parameters: One signed integral microsecond count.
details: Conversion uses integer arithmetic and retains microsecond precision exactly.
The resulting civil year must remain in `1..9999`; no clock is read.
items.errors: `TypeError` for non-integral input and `OutOfRange` for an unsupported result.
items.native: Native C multiplies the exact signed microsecond count with checked arithmetic, normalizes it into seconds plus a non-negative nanosecond field, and returns a UTC `ODatetime` by value.

items.name: parse
items.summary: Parse a datetime with a Go reference-time layout and optional zone context.
items.parameters: A layout `string`, input `string`, and optional `location`. Zone-less input uses UTC unless a location is supplied.
details: Layouts describe field positions with the reference instant `Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006`; `rfc3339` and `rfc3339_nano` cover common interchange.
Numeric offsets in text are preserved as fixed locations. IANA gaps fail and folds choose the earlier instant. Parsing is deterministic.
items.errors: `TypeError` for incompatible arguments, `ParseError` for invalid text, and range errors for unsupported years.

items.name: format
items.summary: Format a datetime in its retained location with a reference-time layout.
items.parameters: One `datetime` and one layout `string`.
details: Write the desired layout using fields from `Mon Jan 2 15:04:05 MST 2006`; for example, `2006-01-02` selects an ISO-style date.
Formatting is pure, does not change the datetime, and never consults the host locale or clock.
items.errors: `TypeError` for incompatible values or `InvalidArgument` for wrong arity.
items.native: Native C formats UTC datetimes through a bounded reference-layout subset, including civil fields, month/weekday names, fractional seconds, and UTC offset tokens. It returns one newly owned string and rejects unsupported values without a capability.

items.name: add
items.summary: Add exact elapsed nanoseconds without changing datetime location identity.
items.parameters: Two durations, or a `datetime` followed by a `duration`.
details: Duration arithmetic is checked and never wraps or saturates.
Adding elapsed time across a DST transition differs intentionally from `add_date`; the operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for an unsupported pair and `OutOfRange` on duration or datetime overflow.

items.name: sub
items.summary: Subtract durations or compute the exact elapsed duration between instants.
items.parameters: Two durations or two datetimes.
details: Datetime subtraction compares instants, regardless of their displayed locations.
The exact result must fit signed 64-bit nanoseconds; this operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for mismatched values and `OutOfRange` when the exact result cannot be represented.

items.name: add_date
items.summary: Apply calendar-relative year, month, and day deltas in the retained location.
items.parameters: One `datetime` and three integral deltas.
details: Calendar normalization follows Go `AddDate`; for example, January 31 plus one month may normalize into March.
A calendar day follows local civil time and can therefore be 23 or 25 elapsed hours across DST.
items.errors: `TypeError` for non-integral arguments and `OutOfRange` when the result leaves years `1..9999`.
items.native: Native C applies checked year/month/day offsets to UTC `ODatetime` values, preserves the time-of-day and nanoseconds, and returns a value-owned datetime without host capability. Negative offsets and years outside `1..9999` are handled explicitly.

items.name: round
items.summary: Round to the nearest non-negative duration quantum.
items.parameters: A `duration` or `datetime` followed by a non-negative `duration` quantum.
details: Duration ties round away from zero. Datetimes round from the zero time while retaining their location.
A zero quantum returns the input. Every result is range-checked and the operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError`, `InvalidArgument` for a negative quantum, or `OutOfRange` for an unrepresentable result.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract for duration and UTC datetime values. Checked integer helpers preserve the year-1 zero-time anchor for arbitrary quanta, require no host capability, allocate no result storage, and retain no input pointer.

items.name: truncate
items.summary: Discard the remainder beyond a non-negative duration quantum.
items.parameters: A `duration` or `datetime` followed by a non-negative `duration` quantum.
details: Negative durations truncate toward zero. Datetimes retain their location.
A zero quantum returns the input; the operation is pure and checked.
items.errors: `TypeError`, `InvalidArgument` for a negative quantum, or `OutOfRange` for an unsupported result.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract for duration and UTC datetime values. Checked integer helpers preserve the year-1 zero-time anchor for arbitrary quanta, require no host capability, allocate no result storage, and retain no input pointer.

items.name: equal
items.summary: Test two durations or two datetime instants for equality.
items.parameters: Two durations or two datetimes of the same kind.
details: Datetime equality compares the instant, not location identity.
The ordinary `==` operator uses the same value rule; this function makes time-specific intent explicit.
items.errors: `TypeError` for mixed or unsupported kinds.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: compares `duration` and UTC `datetime` values without a host capability or allocation.

items.name: before
items.summary: Report whether the left duration or instant precedes the right.
items.parameters: Two durations or two datetimes of the same kind.
details: Datetime ordering uses the represented instant rather than local wall fields.
This operation is deterministic and pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for mixed or unsupported kinds.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: compares `duration` and UTC `datetime` values without a host capability or allocation.

items.name: after
items.summary: Report whether the left duration or instant follows the right.
items.parameters: Two durations or two datetimes of the same kind.
details: Datetime ordering uses the represented instant rather than local wall fields.
This operation is deterministic and pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for mixed or unsupported kinds.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: compares `duration` and UTC `datetime` values without a host capability or allocation.

items.name: compare
items.summary: Three-way compare two durations or two datetime instants.
items.parameters: Two durations or two datetimes of the same kind.
details: The result is `-1i64`, `0i64`, or `1i64`.
Datetime comparison ignores display location and compares the exact instant.
items.errors: `TypeError` for mixed or unsupported kinds.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: compares `duration` and UTC `datetime` values and returns `-1i64`, `0i64`, or `1i64` without a host capability or allocation.

items.name: year
items.summary: Read the civil year in the datetime's retained location.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: The result is in `1..9999`.
Component access is pure and does not alter the instant.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: UTC civil year extraction returns a value-owned `u64` and requires no host capability.

items.name: month
items.summary: Read the civil month number in the retained location.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: January is `1u64` and December is `12u64`.
This operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: UTC civil month extraction returns a value-owned `u64` and requires no host capability.

items.name: day
items.summary: Read the day of the month in the retained location.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: The result is in `1..31` and reflects the local civil representation.
This operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: UTC civil day extraction returns a value-owned `u64` and requires no host capability.

items.name: hour
items.returns: `duration` in value position; `u64` in call position
items.summary: Use the one-hour duration constant or read a datetime's local hour.
items.parameters: No call in value position; one `datetime` in call position.
details: The constant is exactly `3600000000000` nanoseconds. The component result is in `0..23`.
The shared spelling is resolved by value versus call position and remains deterministic after codec round trips.
items.errors: `TypeError` when called with a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C lowers the value-position spelling to an exact one-hour duration and lowers call-position use to UTC hour extraction returning a value-owned `u64` in `0..23`; neither path requires a host capability.

items.name: minute
items.returns: `duration` in value position; `u64` in call position
items.summary: Use the one-minute duration constant or read a datetime's local minute.
items.parameters: No call in value position; one `datetime` in call position.
details: The constant is exactly `60000000000` nanoseconds. The component result is in `0..59`.
The shared spelling is resolved by value versus call position.
items.errors: `TypeError` when called with a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C lowers the value-position spelling to an exact one-minute duration and lowers call-position use to UTC minute extraction returning a value-owned `u64` in `0..59`; neither path requires a host capability.

items.name: second
items.returns: `duration` in value position; `u64` in call position
items.summary: Use the one-second duration constant or read a datetime's local second.
items.parameters: No call in value position; one `datetime` in call position.
details: The constant is exactly `1000000000` nanoseconds. The component result is in `0..59`; leap seconds are not represented.
The shared spelling is resolved by value versus call position.
items.errors: `TypeError` when called with a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C lowers the value-position spelling to an exact one-second duration and lowers call-position use to UTC second extraction returning a value-owned `u64` in `0..59`; neither path requires a host capability.

items.name: nanosecond
items.returns: `duration` in value position; `u64` in call position
items.summary: Use the one-nanosecond duration constant or read a datetime's fractional nanosecond.
items.parameters: No call in value position; one `datetime` in call position.
details: The constant is exactly one nanosecond. The component result is in `0..999999999`.
The shared spelling is resolved by value versus call position.
items.errors: `TypeError` when called with a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C lowers the value-position spelling to an exact one-nanosecond duration and lowers call-position use to UTC nanosecond extraction returning a value-owned `u64` in `0..999999999`; neither path requires a host capability.

items.name: weekday
items.summary: Return the English weekday name in the retained location.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: The stable values are `Sunday` through `Saturday`.
This is not locale-sensitive and does not read the clock.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: UTC weekday extraction returns one of seven static English strings and requires no host capability.

items.name: year_day
items.summary: Return the one-based day within the local civil year.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: The result is `1..365` or `1..366` in a leap year.
This operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C provides this pure-value contract: UTC one-based year-day extraction returns a value-owned `u64` and requires no host capability.

items.name: zone
items.summary: Read the active timezone abbreviation/name and offset.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: The two values are the active zone name and seconds east of UTC.
For an IANA location, the active offset can vary with the instant.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.

items.name: utc
items.summary: Represent the same instant in canonical UTC.
items.parameters: One `datetime`.
details: The instant and nanosecond are unchanged; only retained location identity changes.
This operation is pure.
items.errors: `TypeError` for a non-datetime.
items.native: Native C validates one `datetime` and returns the value-owned UTC `ODatetime` unchanged; the native ABI has no non-UTC location slot, so no host capability, allocation, or input-pointer retention is involved.

items.name: in_location
items.summary: Represent an instant in another fixed or IANA location.
items.parameters: One `datetime` and one `location`.
details: The instant is unchanged; civil components and active offset are recalculated.
Conversion is pure because the location value already contains its rules.
items.errors: `TypeError` for incompatible arguments and `OutOfRange` if the local civil year leaves `1..9999`.

items.name: fixed_zone
items.summary: Create an immutable named timezone with one constant UTC offset.
items.parameters: A non-empty name `string` and integral seconds strictly between `-86400` and `86400`.
details: Fixed locations have no daylight-saving transitions.
The exact name and offset survive binary and JSON serialization.
items.errors: `TypeError`, `InvalidArgument` for an empty name, or `OutOfRange` for an invalid offset.

items.name: load_location
items.summary: Load an immutable IANA timezone by canonical database name.
items.parameters: One non-empty zone name `string`, such as `America/New_York`; `UTC` returns the canonical UTC location.
details: Osiris embeds the timezone snapshot shipped by its Go build toolchain and performs no runtime network fetch.
Hosts and tests can inject a pinned loader through the runtime API.
items.errors: `TypeError`, `InvalidArgument` for an empty name, or `NotFound` when the named zone is unavailable.

items.name: now
items.summary: Read the runtime's explicit clock and return the instant in UTC.
items.parameters: No arguments.
details: This is the only nondeterministic operation in `std/time`; all other functions are pure with respect to the clock.
Tests and deterministic hosts install a clock with `Runtime.SetClock`. The result never retains a host monotonic payload.
items.errors: `InvalidArgument` for unexpected arguments and `OutOfRange` if an injected clock returns an unsupported year.

items.name: rfc3339
items.summary: The standard RFC 3339 layout without a required fractional field.
details: Use it with `parse` and `format` for interoperable offset-bearing timestamps.

items.name: rfc3339_nano
items.summary: The RFC 3339 layout that retains up to nine fractional-second digits.
details: Formatting removes unnecessary trailing fractional zeros without losing represented precision.

items.name: utc_location
items.summary: The canonical zero-offset UTC location.
details: Use it when an API requires an explicit location value.
UTC identity survives codecs and is distinct from an arbitrarily named zero-offset fixed zone.

items.name: microsecond
items.summary: An exact one-microsecond duration constant.
details: The value is `1000` nanoseconds.
It is qualified and does not add or shadow a global measurement-unit name.
items.native: Native C emits the duration payload as a compile-time `INT64_C(1000)` value; it allocates no storage and requires no capability.

items.name: millisecond
items.summary: An exact one-millisecond duration constant.
details: The value is `1000000` nanoseconds.
It is qualified and does not add or shadow a global measurement-unit name.
items.native: Native C emits the duration payload as a compile-time `INT64_C(1000000)` value; it allocates no storage and requires no capability.
